entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please say 'Returns' or 'Product Support' to be routed to the correct department.
Returns.
Connecting you to a returns specialist now.
Thanks for calling VeloFit, my name is Alex. How can I help you today?
Hi, I need to start a return for my last order. The order number is VF90210.
I can certainly help with that. Let me just pull up order VF90210... Okay, I see it here. It looks like you ordered two items: the Pro-Series jersey and the new VeloBand Pulse. Is that correct?
Yes, that's the one. I'd like to return both.

Okay, no problem. Let's start with the jersey. I see the order was delivered five days ago, so you're well within the 90-day window for that. I've just initiated that return for you. You'll receive an email with a pre-paid shipping label shortly.
Great. And what about the Pulse?
For the VeloBand Pulse, can I ask if it has been opened or used?
Well, yeah. I wore it for a couple of days to try it out. The heart rate tracking just isn't accurate for me. That's why I'm returning it.
I see. I'm afraid I can't process a return for the Pulse. Once it has been opened and worn, our policy prevents us from accepting it back for sanitary and resale reasons.
What? That's ridiculous! How am I supposed to know if it works for me if I can't even try it? I'm a VIP member, I've spent thousands here.

I completely understand your frustration, and I truly value your loyalty as a VIP customer. The issue is that we have separate policies for different product categories. Since there were two items in your order, the policy for the jersey is different from the policy for the VeloBand Pulse, which is considered a wearable electronic device.
That was not clear when I bought it! I think your website had a technical error. The page definitely showed the standard 90-day return policy for the whole order. This is a complete bait-and-switch.

I can assure you that's not our intention, and I'm sorry if there was any confusion on the product page. However, the policy on wearable electronics being non-returnable once used is firm. I can't override the physical condition rule.

This is absurd. I have a Whoop band and I returned my first one with zero issues. Peloton would never treat a long-time customer this way. You're telling me I'm just stuck with a $150 piece of plastic?

I do understand, and I want to find a way to make this right. While I absolutely cannot accept the return for the used Pulse, given the potential website confusion and your status as a VIP member, I can offer you a $50 credit on your VeloFit account.
Fifty dollars? You want me to spend more money here after you just refused to refund me for a defective product? I don't want a credit, I want my money back. This is unacceptable.
The $50 credit is the maximum I'm authorized to offer as a goodwill gesture. I've already processed the full refund for the jersey, but for the Pulse, my hands are tied by the policy.
Then get me someone who can help! A supervisor, anyone! This is the worst customer service I have ever experienced.
I can transfer you to my supervisor, but I need to be transparent that they are bound by the same policy regarding used electronics. It's unlikely the outcome will change.

Forget it. Just forget it. I'll dispute the charge with my credit card company and I'll be sure to tell every cycling group I'm in about VeloFit's scam policies. You've lost a customer for life. *click*
I understand your frustration. I will make a note of this on your account... Thank you for calling.
